heading: Prohibition on slaughter of dogs and cats for human consumption

tree.heading: In general
tree.text: Except as provided in subsection (c), no person may—

children.text: knowingly slaughter a dog or cat for human consumption; or
knowingly ship, transport, move, deliver, receive, possess, purchase, sell, or donate—
a dog or cat to be slaughtered for human consumption; or
a dog or cat part for human consumption.

tree.heading: Scope
tree.text: Subsection (a) shall apply only with respect to conduct—

children.text: in or affecting interstate commerce or foreign commerce; or
within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States.

tree.heading: Exception for Indian tribes
tree.text: The prohibition in subsection (a) shall not apply to an Indian (as defined in section 5304 of title 25) carrying out any activity described in subsection (a) for the purpose of a religious ceremony.

tree.heading: Penalty
tree.text: Any person who violates subsection (a) shall be subject to a fine in an amount not greater than $5,000 for each violation.

prevents a State or unit of local government from adopting and enforcing an animal welfare law or regulation that is more stringent than this section.

notes.heading: Codification
notes.text: Section was enacted as part of the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018, and not as part of the Animal Welfare Act which comprises this chapter.
